summary.title: DevSecOps in Kubernetes
summary.one_liner: Learn which security risks span container images, registries, authentication, policy and monitoring in Kubernetes/AKS, and the DevSecOps practices that mitigate them.
takeaways: Container stacks have many layers (orchestrator, host OS, runtime, images, registry, running containers), each needing security.
Scan images in CI/CD, avoid clear-text secrets by using Kubernetes Secrets or Key Vault, and allow only validated or signed images.
Restrict registry access with namespaces, dedicated virtual networks, limited individual identities, service principals for pipelines, and content trust.
Integrate Azure Active Directory with AKS, enable MFA, use service accounts for CI/CD, and apply conditional access policies.
Use Azure policy on AKS for deploy-time enforcement and Azure Monitor and Security Center for alerting on security drift.
summary.summary: The Microsoft Open Source Blog post argues that DevSecOps should make security a shared responsibility across the application lifecycle, and explains why this matters as Kubernetes adoption grows. It walks through risk areas in order: container images, container registries, authentication and authorization, policy control for pipelines and clusters, and alerting and monitoring. Each section lists practical mitigations, using Azure services such as Azure Container Registry, AKS, Azure Active Directory, Key Vault, Azure Monitor and Security Center as examples. The post closes with a summary and links to related Microsoft DevSecOps resources.
